function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most anticipated festivals happening soon in the United States—along with a few practical tips on how to plan your trip and snag tickets.

| Festival | Dates | Location | What to Expect | Ticket Info |
|----------|-------|----------|----------------|-------------|
| **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | March 8–17, 2026 | Austin, TX | Music, film, interactive media, panels, networking events. | Early‑bird tickets start at $199 (online). Check the official SXSW site for updates. |
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | April 14–18, 2026 | New Orleans, LA | Live jazz, blues, zydeco, Cajun, world music, food stalls, art exhibits. | General admission $75 (online). VIP packages $200+. |
| **Burning Man** | Aug 27–Sep 5, 2026 | Black Rock Desert, NV | Art installations, music camps, community-driven culture, “Leave No Trace” ethos. | Tickets $350 (online). Limited availability—buy early. |
| **Sundance Film Festival** | Jan 19–29, 2026 | Park City, UT | Premieres of independent films, panels, industry networking. | Early‑bird passes $125 (online). |
| **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | Apr 20–22 & Apr 27–29, 2026 | Indio, CA | Top-tier music acts, art installations, fashion, food trucks. | General admission $499 (online). VIP $1,099. |

### How to Get Tickets

1. **Official Websites** – Always buy directly from the festival’s own site. Look for “Tickets” or “Buy Now” buttons.  
2. **Early‑Bird Sales** – Most festivals release early‑bird tickets weeks before the event. Sign up for newsletters to receive alerts.  
3. **Resale Platforms** – If you miss early sales, reputable resale sites like Ticketmaster Resale or StubHub often have legitimate tickets. Verify authenticity before purchasing.  
4. **Social Media & Email Alerts** – Follow the festival’s official Twitter, Instagram, and Facebook pages. They’ll announce flash sales or last‑minute deals.  

### Planning Tips

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Book Accommodation Early** | Hotels near festival venues fill up fast—especially in cities like Austin and New Orleans. |
| **Check Weather Forecasts** | Festivals in desert or coastal areas can be hot or rainy. Pack accordingly. |
| **Transportation** | Consider carpooling or using rideshare services to avoid parking hassles. |
| **Pack Essentials** | Sunscreen, reusable water bottle, portable charger, and a small backpack for day‑time gear. |
| **Know the Rules** | Some festivals (e.g., Burning Man) have strict “Leave No Trace” policies—read them ahead of time. |

---

#### Quick Links

- **SXSW** – https://www.sxsw.com/tickets/
- **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** – https://www.nojazzfest.com/tickets/
- **Burning Man** – https://burningman.org/tickets/
- **Sundance Film Festival** – https://www.sundance.org/festivals/sundance-film-festival
- **Coachella** – https://www.coachella.com/tickets/

Let me know if you’d like more details on a specific festival, or if you’re looking for something niche (food, tech, literary, etc.). Happy planning!
